chunks: They rejoined: "We feel you augur ill. If you do not desist, we shall stone you to death, and inflict a grievous punishment on you."

key_terms.تَطَيَّرْنَا: We felt augured ill / We considered you bringers of bad omens
key_terms.لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهُوا: If you do not desist / cease

ai.seo_question: What did the people say to the prophets regarding their preaching and what punishment did they threaten?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological mechanism of 'superstition' (tatayyur) used by the disbelievers to dismiss divine signs as mere omens of misfortune. The threat of stoning reflects the pre-Islamic Arab practice of executing prophets for disrupting social order, while the 'painful punishment' alludes to the specific historical afflictions that befell their city. This narrative serves as a paradigm for how communities reject truth when it challenges their entrenched traditions.
